newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for leads.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Wednesday with most consumers seen glued to the sidelines waiting for leads in the afternoon session, dealers said.
"There were no trades this morning and people are just waiting for leads from Japan later in the day. We also want to see if some shortcovering will come in," a dealer said.
"The big boys were not in at the moment. They'll bide their time as usual and wait for the last few hours of trade before possibly coming in," a trader added.
Traders said they were looking to see if Michelin and Bridgestone, which were said to have sought quotes from the trade recently, may come back into the market.
"The buyers will probably try to ask for quotes again, but you're not sure if they would really buy," a dealer said.
Prices in the market were marked slightly easier in line with softer prices in Tokyo and Kobe, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 94.50 U.S. cents a kg from 95.25 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 139.00 Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg from 139.50 cents.
